 Prediction: UNT will roll past Rice, set up a monster showdown with UTSA 
 By Brett Vito Staff Writer 
 Brett Vito 
 UNT Athletics reporter
 Author twitter 
 Author email 
 Nov 5, 2026 
 Nov 5, 2026 
 Updated 
 5 hrs ago 
 Comments 
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 WhatsApp 
 SMS 
 Email 
 North Texas quarterback Tayven Jackson and the Mean Green will face Rice in their homecoming game on Saturday at DATCU Stadium.
 Marco Barrera/For the DRC 
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 WhatsApp 
 SMS 
 Email 
 Print 
 Copy article link 
 Save 
 Rice at North Texas
 When: 3 p.m. Saturday
 Where: DATCU Stadium, Denton
 Records: UNT 6-2, 4-0 American; Rice 1-7, 0-4 American
 Last game: UNT 48, Florida Atlantic 41; Florida Atlantic 51, Rice 49
 Last matchup: UNT 56, Rice 24 (2025)
 TV: ESPNU
 What’s at stake?
 North Texas is tied with UTSA atop the American Conference standings at 4-0 after winning its fifth straight game.
 The Mean Green and Roadrunners will face off in the Alamodome on Nov. 14. The game will be huge no matter what happens this week, but both teams are looking to make it a showdown of teams that are unbeaten in league play.
 UNT can get there with a win over Rice. UTSA has an even more challenging game at Florida Atlantic late Thursday night.
 Mean Green coach Neal Brown and his players have vowed not to overlook Rice, a team that has come close to breaking through for its second win of the season several times this year.
 Meeting that goal would move UNT another step closer to winning a conference title.
 The Owls head into their showdown with the Mean Green aiming for a landmark win late in the season when nothing has gone right.
 When UNT has the ball
 UNT has been one of the best offensive teams in the country all season and has scored at least 45 points in every game it has played since a loss to Texas State in the third week of the year.
 The Mean Green rank second nationally with an average of 43.8 points per game. Only Miami is putting up more at 47.6.
 UNT’s success has been due in large part to the combination of quarterback Tayven Jackson and running back Jahiem White. Jackson ranks third nationally with 2,577 passing yards, while White is sitting second in rushing yards with 1,047.
 Rice is allowing 31.8 points per game.
 When Rice has the ball
 UNT put together one of its best defensive outings of the season when it held Charlotte to 10 points in a win back on Oct. 10.
 That game represented a high point in what has been an up-and-down year that has seen the Mean Green allow 31.9 points per game.
 Linebacker Zakye Baker and safety CJ Coombes have both played key roles for the Mean Green. Barker leads UNT with 62 tackles, while Coombes has added 56 stops.
 UNT will need the pair of veterans to play key roles in shutting down Rice’s option attack and quarterback Jacurri Brown. The Georgia native played at both Miami and Central Florida and is a high-end talent as well as a dual-threat player.
 Brown has rushed for 660 yards and thrown for an additional 478. Rice’s offense goes as Brown goes.
 Prediction
 UNT has won games in a variety of ways during its five-game winning streak. The Mean Green pulled out an overtime game against Tulsa and blew out Charlotte.
 UNT shouldn’t have a whole lot of trouble with Rice, as long as it doesn’t get caught looking ahead to its game against UTSA.
 The Mean Green have far too much offensive firepower for Rice to handle. UNT also recently played another team that relies on an option offense in Navy.
 That experience should pay dividends for UNT.
 Score: UNT 49, Rice 21
